sections.section_title: Clinical Presentation and Pathophysiological Context of Abdominal Masses in Pregnancy
sections.description: This section establishes the clinical background required to understand the presentation of large pelvic masses during the second trimester. It covers the physiological changes of pregnancy on uterine smooth muscle, the typical incidence of leiomyomas, and how they present as atypical symptoms (pain, dyspnea, mass effect) versus classic benign progression.
subtopics: Physiological uterine growth and leiomyoma behavior during pregnancy
Presentation of complications: abdominal pain and mechanical dyspnea
Clinical examination findings: abdominal distension and bimanual assessment
Initial laboratory abnormalities: anemia, infection markers, and differential significance of fever

sections.section_title: Diagnostic Reasoning: Imaging Interpretation, Markers, and Differential Diagnosis
sections.description: Detailed examination of the diagnostic workup used to distinguish between ovarian cysts, endometriomas, and uterine leiomyomas. This section focuses on the utility of ultrasound and non-contrast MRI in pregnancy, interpreting specific imaging features, and managing serum tumor markers in the context of pregnancy physiology.
subtopics: Ultrasound characteristics: cystic vs. solid components and vascularity
Role of MRI in differentiating myoma location and interfaces with the cavity
Interpretation of CA-125 levels during different trimesters of pregnancy
Differential diagnosis of decidualized endometriomas vs. cystic degenerating leiomyomas
Limitations and pitfalls of serum tumor markers in pregnancy

sections.section_title: Surgical Management and Decision-Making in the Second Trimester
sections.description: An in-depth analysis of the intraoperative management of the identified pathology. This section explains the rationale for choosing laparotomy over conservative management at this gestation, the surgical technique chosen (myomectomy vs. observation), and the handling of specific complications like torsion and leakage.
subtopics: Indications for surgical intervention: complications versus expectant management
Surgical approach: open vs. laparoscopic considerations for high-gestational age
Technique of myomectomy in pregnant patients: clamping, resection, and closure
Intra-operative management of bleeding, infection, and fetal monitoring
Rationale for partial resection and leaving specific masses in situ

sections.section_title: Obstetric Delivery Planning and Intra-operative Hematologic Support
sections.description: This section covers the planning for fetal and maternal delivery in the context of residual masses. It addresses how the size and location of the retained mass impact the mode of delivery, the management of anemia and infection post-surgery, and the timing of the caesarean section.
subtopics: Impact of uterine masses on fetal presentation and expulsive phase
Timing of elective caesarean section relative to residual myoma size
Hematologic management: transfusion thresholds and iron supplementation
Antibiotic stewardship for secondary UTI infection during pregnancy
Intra-operative pharmacologic prophylaxis for preterm labor

sections.section_title: Postoperative Course and Long-term Clinical Implications
sections.description: A comprehensive review of the outcome, follow-up, and the broader clinical lessons derived from the management of atypical abdominal masses. This section discusses maternal recovery, fetal well-being, lactation, and strategies for future management of uterine fibroids.
subtopics: Maternal recovery metrics: wound healing, infection monitoring, and elimination of symptoms
Fetal well-being and growth assessment: amniotic fluid and growth charts
Mechanics of postpartum fibroid regression during pregnancy
Future management decisions regarding myomectomy vs. observation postpartum
Clinical pearls: balancing maternal quality of life with obstetric safety
